title: Top cohomology of a derived adjunct and the local direct-image edge
statement:
Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with module derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], derived pullback and direct image [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image], and the canonical derived adjunction $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$ normalized by the single-module transpose of [lem-pc-canonical-single-adjunction-transpose]. Let $q\in\mathbf Z$, $C\in D(\mathcal O_S)$ satisfy $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>q$, and let $K\in D^+(\mathcal O_T)$, meaning $H^i(K)=0$ for all sufficiently negative $i$. Write $\kappa_{g,C}:H^q(Lg^*C)\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*H^q(C)$ for [lem-weil-pbc-derived-pullback-top-cohomology], using ordinary tensor pullback and its adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. For every derived object $E$ on a scheme $Y$, let $\Theta^E_V:H^q(V,E)\to\Gamma(V,H^qE)$ be the canonical local-class map of [lem-pc-ringed-space-sheafification-cohomology]. Let $\lambda_{g,K,V}:H^q(V,Rg_*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(g^{-1}V,K)$ be the canonical local derived-sections comparison [lem-trf-unbounded-direct-image-section-presheaf]. Define $e^q_{g,K}:H^q(Rg_*K)\to g_*H^q(K)$ by sheafifying the morphism of module presheaves with components $\Theta^K_{g^{-1}V}\lambda_{g,K,V}$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; thus $\Gamma(V,e^q_{g,K})\Theta^{Rg_*K}_V=\Theta^K_{g^{-1}V}\lambda_{g,K,V}$. Then for every $d:Lg^*C\to K$ and its derived adjunct $\alpha:C\to Rg_*K$, the ordinary adjunct of $H^q(d)\kappa_{g,C}^{-1}:g^*H^q(C)\to H^q(K)$ is exactly
$$e^q_{g,K}H^q(\alpha):H^q(C)\longrightarrow g_*H^q(K).$$
The truncations and cohomology here are for the standard t-structures [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0BKJ, cohomology-lemma-sheafification-cohomology, canonical local-class map. Agent top-cohomology adjunct refinement, using the normalized single-module transpose and standard truncations cited in the statement; the adjunct equality is not asserted verbatim by this tag.

proof.text:
First record naturality of the edge as defined in the statement. For a derived morphism $t:E\to E'$ on $T$, naturality of the local-class map and of the local derived-sections comparison gives, on every open $V\subseteq S$,
$\Theta^{E'}_{g^{-1}V}\lambda_{g,E',V}H^q(V,Rg_*t)=\Gamma(g^{-1}V,H^q(t))\Theta^E_{g^{-1}V}\lambda_{g,E,V}$.
Sheafify this equality. The universal property of module sheafification gives
$e^q_{g,E'}H^q(Rg_*t)=g_*H^q(t)e^q_{g,E}$.
All maps are module-linear: on $V$ their scalar action is restricted along $g^\sharp_V$.

For any $\mathcal O_T$-module $M$, write $u_{g,M,q}:(g_*M)[-q]\to Rg_*(M[-q])$ for the canonical single direct-image comparison, shifted from degree zero using the recorded direct-image shift structure. Its edge normalization is
$e^q_{g,M[-q]}H^q(u_{g,M,q})=\mathrm{id}_{g_*M}$.
Here is the local calculation specifying this equality. Choose a K-injective resolution $r:M[-q]\to I$. On this model the comparison is $g_*r$, and a section $m\in M(g^{-1}V)$ goes to the cocycle $r^q(m)$ in $I^q(g^{-1}V)$. Under the local comparison $\lambda$ this is the same cocycle, and $\Theta$ takes its class to the image of $m$ under $H^q(r):M\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(I)$. Identifying back along $H^q(r)$ gives $m$. This proves the identity on every section of $g_*M$ and hence on the sheaf. Shifting both complexes only changes differentials by a common sign, which changes neither this cycle nor its quotient class.

source.place: Tags 079W (lemma-adjoint: K-injective construction), 0D5X and 0BKJ, with the explicit single direct-image comparison

proof.text:
Put $A=Lg^*C$, $N=H^q(C)$, $M=H^q(K)$, and $J=\tau_{\ge q}K$, with projection $j:K\to J$. Thus $H^q(j)$ is the identity after the canonical identification $H^q(J)=M$. Good truncation gives a canonical $i:M[-q]\to J$ inducing that same identity: $\tau_{\le q}J$ is canonically quasi-isomorphic to $M[-q]$, and $i$ is its inclusion into $J$. Indeed, in a complex representing $J$ with no terms below $q$, this is the inclusion of $\ker(d_J^q)$ in degree $q$. The canonical triangle at $q+1$ gives
$M[-q]\xrightarrow{i}J\to J_1\to M[-q+1]$, where $J_1=\tau_{\ge q+1}J\in D^{\ge q+1}$.
The pullback top-cohomology theorem gives $A\in D^{\le q}$. Its canonical triangle at $q$ is
$A_0\to A\xrightarrow{\tau_A}H^q(A)[-q]\to A_0[1]$, with $A_0=\tau_{\le q-1}A\in D^{\le q-1}$. These identifications follow from the displayed kernels and cokernels in good truncation and hold for unbounded derived objects.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), at a=q-1 and a=q; Homology Tag 0118 (section-truncations)

proof.text: For any $h:A\to J$, orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A_0,J)=0$, since $A_0\le q-1$ and $J\ge q$. Exactness of contravariant Hom on the source triangle of step 3 therefore gives $h=\ell\tau_A$ for some $\ell:H^q(A)[-q]\to J$. Orthogonality also gives $\operatorname{Hom}(H^q(A)[-q],J_1)=0$, since the bounds are $q$ and $q+1$. Exactness of covariant Hom on the target triangle gives $\ell=i b'$ with $b':H^q(A)[-q]\to M[-q]$.

source.place: Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological), applied to the two triangles of step 3; standard t-structure orthogonality

proof.text: Full faithfulness of the single-complex embedding, shifted by $-q$, writes $b'=b[-q]$ for a unique module map $b:H^q(A)\to M$. Applying $H^q$ to $h=i b[-q]\tau_A$ shows $b=H^q(h)$, because both $i$ and $\tau_A$ induce the canonical identity in degree $q$. Consequently two morphisms $A\to J$ with the same $H^q$ are equal. This is just the two factorizations of step 4 and full faithfulness; it makes no assertion that cohomology is faithful on the whole derived category.

proof.text:
Let $a=H^q(d)\kappa_{g,C}^{-1}:g^*N\to M$, and let $b:N\to g_*M$ be its ordinary adjunct. Define
$v:Lg^*C\xrightarrow{Lg^*\tau_C}Lg^*(N[-q])\xrightarrow{c_{g,N}[-q]}(g^*N)[-q]$,
where the displayed second arrow includes the canonical pullback shift comparison. By the normalized formula for $\kappa_{g,C}$, $H^q(v)=\kappa_{g,C}$. Thus $jd$ and $i a[-q]v$ are morphisms $A\to J$ with the same degree-$q$ map, namely $H^q(d)$ under $H^q(J)=M$. Step 5 gives
$jd=i a[-q]v$.

source.place: Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), dual top-degree truncation comparison; Cohomology Tag 0D5S for the pinned pullback shifts

proof.text:
Transpose the last equation under the selected derived adjunction. To identify the comparison maps precisely, apply the single-module transpose theorem with the identity of $g^*N$: its pullback comparison has transpose the ordinary unit followed by the single direct-image comparison. This is also the defining normalization of $c_{g,N}$ in the top-cohomology theorem. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection therefore identifies these two pullback comparisons. The single-module transpose theorem says that the adjunct of $a[0]c_{g,N}$ is $u_{g,M,0}b[0]$. The pinned derived adjunction commutes with shifts, and the pullback counit commutes with those same shifts, so the shifted equality says that the adjunct of $a[-q]c_{g,N}[-q]$ is $u_{g,M,q}b[-q]$. Bifunctoriality of the adjunction, first with the source map $\tau_C$ and then with the target map $i$, now gives the explicit equation
$Rg_*(j)\alpha=Rg_*(i)\,u_{g,M,q}\,b[-q]\,\tau_C$.
This uses the fixed single-module normalization in the statement; it does not choose a new adjunction.

source.place: Tag 079W (lemma-adjoint); normalized single-module transpose and its pinned integer-shift compatibility

proof.text:
Apply $H^q$ to step 7 and compose with $e^q_{g,J}$. By step 1 with $t=j$, the left side is $g_*H^q(j)e^q_{g,K}H^q(\alpha)$, identified with $e^q_{g,K}H^q(\alpha)$. By step 1 with $t=i$ and step 2, the first two factors on the right satisfy
$e^q_{g,J}H^q(Rg_*i)H^q(u_{g,M,q})=g_*H^q(i)e^q_{g,M[-q]}H^q(u_{g,M,q})=\mathrm{id}_{g_*M}$.
Also $H^q(\tau_C)$ is the canonical identity on $N$. The resulting equality is therefore $e^q_{g,K}H^q(\alpha)=b$, exactly the ordinary adjunct required. Every use of an identification here has its degree-$q$ map specified in steps 2, 3 and 6.
